Fit lag sequential analysis models at several lags

Source: R/lsa-lags.R
lsa_lags.Rd

lsa_lags() fits lsa() once per requested lag, with the same engine and options, and keeps the fits together. The result is a lag profile in the sense of Sackett (1979), who proposed examining a transition across a range of lags to separate short-range from longer-range dependence and to detect cycles: a sequential contingency need not be immediate, a state may tend to recur two or three events later, and an association that is strong at lag 1 may fade with distance.

transitions() on the result stacks the per-lag transition tables into one table with a lag column, with the same filtering and sorting arguments as for a single fit. To follow one transition across lags, use lag_profile().

Usage

lsa_lags(data, lags = 1:3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_lags'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_lags'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

data

Sequences in any form accepted by lsa().

lags

Integer vector of lags (default 1:3). Negative lags look back to predecessors.

...

Passed to lsa() (for example engine, alpha, loops). Ignored by the print() and as.data.frame() methods.

x

An lsa_lags object.

row.names

Optional row names for the stacked data frame.

optional

Ignored; present for consistency with the generic.

Value

An object of class c("lsa_lags", "list"), one lsa fit per lag. transitions() and as.data.frame() return a data.frame with one row per transition and lag and the columns of transitions() for a single fit. print() lists the number of significant transitions at each lag and returns x invisibly.

References

Sackett, G. P. (1979). The lag sequential analysis of contingency and cyclicity in behavioral interaction research. In J. D. Osofsky (Ed.), Handbook of infant development (pp. 623-649). Wiley.

See also

lag_profile() for one transition across lags; lsa(); transitions().

Examples

prof <- lsa_lags(engagement, lags = 1:3)
prof
#> <lsa_lags>
#>   engine: classical
#>   lags:   1, 2, 3
#>     lag 1    7 of 9 transitions significant
#>     lag 2    8 of 9 transitions significant
#>     lag 3    8 of 9 transitions significant
transitions(prof, direction = "over", sort = "strength")
